sections.heading: Understanding WebP and JPG Format Differences
paragraphs: WebP supports both lossy and lossless compression, giving it a flexibility that JPG does not offer. Lossy WebP achieves smaller files than JPG at comparable visual quality by using a more advanced prediction model, while lossless WebP preserves every pixel at a fraction of PNG's size.

Transparency and animation are first-class citizens in WebP. JPG cannot handle either, which means images with transparent backgrounds or frame-based animation lose those properties during conversion. Planning ahead for this trade-off avoids surprises when the output looks different from the source.

JPG remains the safest format for photographic content because virtually every device, platform and application renders it correctly. The format's ubiquity outweighs WebP's efficiency advantages whenever broad compatibility is the priority rather than minimal file size.

sections.heading: When to Keep WebP Instead of Converting
paragraphs: If the destination platform supports WebP natively, converting to JPG adds unnecessary file size without visual benefit. Modern browsers, Google Workspace and many design tools handle WebP perfectly well.

WebP's smaller file sizes improve page load times and reduce bandwidth costs for websites serving large image galleries. Converting these back to JPG for a project that will ultimately re-optimize them adds an extra generation of quality loss.

The decision comes down to the audience. Internal teams with modern tools can work in WebP directly, while external distribution to diverse systems almost always benefits from the universal reach of JPG.

faqs.q: What happens to transparency when converting to JPG?
faqs.a: JPG does not support transparency, so transparent areas are typically rendered against a white background. Plan for this when converting WebP images with alpha channels.

faqs.q: Can I convert multiple WebP files at once?
faqs.a: Yes. The tool supports processing multiple files in sequence so you can convert an entire batch without repeated manual uploads.

faqs.q: Should I convert to JPG or keep WebP for my website?
faqs.a: If your audience uses modern browsers, WebP offers smaller files and faster loads. For email campaigns, print or legacy systems, JPG provides universal compatibility.
